correctness.rationale: The 20-vertex graph is explicitly defined in two standard isomorphic models. All 20 singleton, 190 pair and 1140 triple candidates are evaluated by terminating monotone power-domination closure. Exactly 240 triples succeed; they have distance signatures (2,3,5) and (3,3,4), 120 each. The S5×C2 action is explicitly enumerated and acts transitively on each type. Exact reconfiguration adjacency uses one exchanged vertex with/without adjacency in the base graph. BFS from each symmetry orbit and full all-pairs Floyd–Warshall in an independently coded GP(10,3) solver give the same complete spectrum; 60 diameter-eight pairs match the explicit involution. No infinite inference or untested algorithmic premise is used.

value.rationale: Power domination models minimal placement of network observability sensors; relocating minima while never losing full observability is mathematically natural. On this canonical 20-vertex distance-transitive cubic graph the entire optimum state space is classified by two intrinsic graph-distance signatures. Although the slide graph is 4-regular on both types, its two orbits have sharp different eccentricities (7 and 8); the type-8 part has a unique farthest partner given by an involution on K4 perfect matchings. This nonobvious exact structural obstruction and complete shortest-path distribution form a reproducible reference problem, not a routine restatement of the known power-domination bound.
